about.title: A family tradition of electrical excellence.
text: Cross Electric's story began in 1980 and has continued through three generations of electrical experience. Over the years the company has grown while remaining rooted in the values that built it: quality workmanship, dependable service and taking care of customers.
Today Cross Electric is owned and operated by Brandon and Jen Cross, who lead a team dedicated to providing dependable electrical service with professionalism, skill and pride in their work.
More than 46 years after Cross Electric began, that family tradition remains at the heart of everything we do, from our electricians in the field to the team supporting them behind the scenes.

faqs.q: How much does Cross Club cost?
faqs.a: Cross Club is a monthly membership currently priced at $9.95 per month.

faqs.q: What is included with my membership?
faqs.a: Membership includes an annual whole-home electrical safety evaluation, priority service, discounts, extended warranty protection and exclusive member specials.

faqs.q: How often is the electrical safety evaluation performed?
faqs.a: The membership includes an annual whole-home electrical safety evaluation.

faqs.q: Do Cross Club members receive priority service?
faqs.a: Yes. Cross Club members receive front-of-the-line priority service when they need electrical assistance.

faqs.q: Do Cross Club members receive extra warranty benefits?
faqs.a: Cross Club members receive a lifetime warranty on installations, and double the warranty on repairs.

faqs.q: What if I sell my home?
faqs.a: Your membership is transferable to the new owner if you sell your home. Your membership plan can also move with you to your new home if you stay in our service area.

faqs.q: Do you offer emergency electrical service?
faqs.a: Yes. Cross Electric provides 24-hour emergency electrical service for homes and businesses when an electrical problem cannot wait for business hours.

faqs.q: Does my electrical panel need to be replaced?
faqs.a: Not always. Breakers that trip often, lights that dim when appliances run, a panel that feels hot or smells unusual, a home still on fuses or a Federal Pacific panel are all reasons to have it evaluated. We look at whether a repair will solve the problem before recommending replacement.
